Object-sensitivity is widely used as a context abstraction for computing the points-to information context-sensitively for object-oriented languages like Java. Due to the combinatorial explosion of contexts in large programs,

While already effective, these heuristics-based pre-analyses do not provide precision guarantees, and consequently, are limited in the efficiency gains achieved. We introduce a radically different approach, Eagle, that makes
            k

result.paraphrase: Object sensitivity is commonly used as a context abstraction to compute points-to information context-sensitively for object-oriented languages such as Java. But because contexts explode combinatorially in large programs, k-object-sensitive pointer analysis (under k-limiting), written as k-obj, scales only for small k values, typically k ≤ 2. Some recent approaches try to make it more efficient by having k-obj analyze only certain methods context-sensitively, with those methods chosen heuristically by a pre-analysis. Although effective to a degree, these heuristic pre-analyses offer no precision guarantees and therefore limit the efficiency improvements they can achieve. We present a fundamentally different approach, Eagle, which makes k-obj run much faster than prior methods while preserving precision. Eagle’s key idea is to let k-obj analyze a method with partial context-sensitivity, meaning it is context-sensitive for only some selected variables or allocation sites. It chooses these selections in a lightweight pre-analysis by reasoning about context-free-language (CFL) reachability at the level of variables and objects in the program, using a new CFL-reachability formulation of k-obj. We show Eagle’s progress by comparing it with prior art on a set of popular Java benchmarks and applications.
